purpose: Offline fixtures for bfinance.screener, the package's backbone fundamentals source. Every file is a verbatim recording of a live screener.in response, except where trim_rule says otherwise. Trimmed regions are listed per file. Captured in two sessions on 2026-09-27 UTC: the six company/peers/chart files at ~16:28, the three /market/ files at ~18:21-18:23; each file's own captured_at_utc is authoritative.
robots: screener.in/robots.txt disallows /user/*, /*?q=, /*?sort=, /*?limit=, /*?page= and /company/source/quarter/*. The robots-disallowed search route /api/company/search/?q= was never called, the chart API was recorded with companyId= first so the query string does not begin with q=, and robots.txt itself was re-read live before the /market/ fetches. No ?page= or ?limit= URL was ever requested - the leaf pages carry such links and they were deliberately left alone, which is why the constituent list is partial by construction. Requests were paced at >= 1.2 s.

market.html.trim_rule: the single table.striped.data-table kept verbatim, re-wrapped in a bare <html><body>. Nothing inside it was touched: all 201 <tr>, all 188 leaf hrefs, all ten <td> per industry row and all 752 percent <span class="sub"> survive. Dropped: <head>, nav, footer, and every <script>. This is the whole of what parse_market_industries reads - it selects nothing outside this table - and the trim was proved behaviour-neutral by parsing the raw 177,020-byte response and this fixture and comparing the full frame (values, index, dtypes) and frame.attrs with pandas.testing.assert_frame_equal.
market.html.notes: An unadvertised entry point: linked from no company page and from no top-nav item; only the typed URL reaches it. The request carries NO query string, so none of the six robots.txt rules (every one of which needs a `?`) can match it. Measured shape: 201 <tr> = 13 repeated header rows + 188 leaf industries; there is no <thead>, and the single <tbody> contains the header rows AND the data rows together, so it separates nothing - which is why the parser requires BOTH a /market/ leaf link and exactly ten <td> on a row. The 188 leaves' own `No. of Companies` column sums to 3,319 - the most conservative of the three company-count universes screener.in publishes for the same nodes (the leaf pages' own `results found` sums to 5,468, the browse dropdown's child count to 7,068; the filters behind each are undetermined and the three disagree for individual nodes - Pharmaceuticals reports 159 here and 218 on its own leaf page).

company_itc_full_columns.html.notes: THE ANSWER FIXTURE for 'does screener.in publish quarterly balance sheet and quarterly cash flow?'. NO - it does not. Measured on this file: section#quarters has 13 period columns, 'Jun 2023'..'Jun 2026', months {Jun,Sep,Dec,Mar}, NO 'TTM' column, and its rows are P&L only (Sales, Expenses, Operating Profit, OPM %, Other Income, Interest, Depreciation, Profit before tax, Tax %, Net Profit, EPS in Rs, Raw PDF) - zero balance-sheet or cash-flow line items. section#balance-sheet and section#cash-flow each have 12 period columns, 'Mar 2015'..'Mar 2026', EVERY one of them 'Mar' (fiscal year end), with no non-Mar column and no 'TTM'. So balance sheet and cash flow are annual only. Note section#profit-loss ALSO carries a trailing 'TTM' column after its 12 annual ones, so 'TTM' marks the annual P&L table, not a quarterly section. Recorded because company_itc.html cut every one of these tables to the trailing 2 columns (['Mar 2025','Mar 2026'] for balance sheet and cash flow, ['Mar 2026','Jun 2026'] for quarters), which is what made the question unanswerable from the fixtures. Section id sequence here matches company_itc.html exactly.
